ops.title: Three supervision tests sample alive(pid) once after Close — a signal-delivery vs reaped-exit race that only loses under load
ops.premise:
Suspicion: TestOwnedCloseDrainsARunChildsDescendants (own_test.go:509),
TestOwnedCloseDoesNotPinAnInFlightRunToItsOwnDeadline (own_test.go:566), and
TestConsumerCLIScopeReclaimsAPriorGeneration (acceptance_test.go:163) each sample alive(pid) ONCE,
immediately after Close/reclaim returns. Signal delivery is not process reaping, so the sample can
land in the window between them. That is a race by construction, not a mystery.

Measured 2026-08-02 on the merged Lane D tree:
- Unloaded, targeted: scripts/test.sh -race -count=20 over all three = 60 executions,
  ZERO failures, exit 0, 247s. So the tests are clean when the machine is idle.
- Under load: a Lane D refuter saw one of three full-suite runs go red on exactly these three,
  with a foreign cargo test suite running concurrently. Earlier in the same phase, concurrent
  lanes drove the disk to 100% and produced unrelated failures, so this machine under fan-out is
  a genuinely contended environment.
- CI on main is green across every run of this phase.

So: reproduces only under CPU contention, and the contention source in every observation was other
agents on this machine rather than anything in the repo.

Neither file was touched by the wire-hardening or business lanes (last substantive touch 1b031f7,
a prior phase), so this is pre-existing and orthogonal to the phase-4 surface.

Two candidate resolutions, and they are not equivalent:
(b) Poll alive(pid) to a bound instead of sampling once. Pure test change, no production
    semantics move. Cheap and obviously correct for an asynchronous condition.
(c) Make Owned.Close prove reaping before it returns. Changes what Close guarantees to every
    consumer — a stronger contract, and an owner decision, not a test fix.

(b) is almost certainly right: the tests assert a property Close does not currently promise. But if
the intent was that Close DOES promise it, then the tests are correct and the production code is
the defect — which is why this is an investigation and not a papercut.

Not a v0.21.0 tag blocker on the evidence: 0/60 unloaded plus green CI. Recorded so a random red
on a release commit is recognized rather than re-diagnosed.
